rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Manthūr transmits the preceding interpretation through several routes from Ibn ʿAbbās and others.
rows.anchor: وروي هذا المعنى في الدر المنثور بطرق عن ابن عباس وغيره.

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: They say this was the first verse revealed about fighting; the Prophet fought those who fought him and refrained from those who refrained until 9:5 was revealed and abrogated it.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع أيضا عن الربيع بن أنس وعبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم هذه أول آية نزلت في القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī rejects their abrogation claim as conjecture: the verse is not abrogated but a general ruling follows an earlier specific one.
rows.anchor: أقول وهذا اجتهاد منهما وقد عرفت أن الآية غير ناسخة للآية بل هو من قبيل تعميم الحكم بعد خصوصه.

rows.speaker: المجمع
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ reports that 2:191 was revealed after a Companion killed a disbeliever during a sacred month and believers were criticized; God clarified that religious persecution is graver, though fighting then is forbidden.
rows.anchor: وفي المجمع في قوله تعالى { واقتلوهم حيث ثقفتموهم } الآية نزلت في سبب رجل من الصحابة قتل رجلا من الكفار في الشهر الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent unity of the passage indicates that these verses were revealed together.
rows.anchor: وقد عرفت ان ظاهر وحدة السياق في الآيات الشريفة أنها نزلت دفعة واحدة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda explains fitna as shirk and says fighting continues until worship belongs to God, expressed by the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: بطرق عن قتادة، قال وقاتلوهم حتى لا تكون فتنة أي شرك ويكون الدين لله.

rows.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Qatāda transmits the Prophet saying God commanded him to fight people until they profess the testimony; once they stop, aggression is only against wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: وذكر لنا أن النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم كان يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement identifying the wrongdoer as one refusing the testimony is Qatāda’s inference from the Prophet’s words, and al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī considers it sound.
rows.anchor: أقول قوله وإن الظالم من قول قتادة، استفاد ذلك من قول النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم وهي استفادة حسنة

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: A similar interpretation is also reported from ʿIkrima.
rows.anchor: وروي نظير ذلك عن عكرمة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: During the conflict of Ibn al-Zubayr, Ibn ʿUmar answered two men urging him to fight that God had forbidden his brother’s blood; they cited the command to fight until fitna ended, and he answered that their fighting would restore fitna and turn religion away from God.
rows.anchor: أخرج البخاري وأبو الشيخ وابن مردويه عن ابن عمر إنه أتاه رجلان في فتنة ابن الزبير فقالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī says Ibn ʿUmar misunderstood fitna, and the two questioners misunderstood it as well.
rows.anchor: أقول وقد أخطأ في معنى الفتنة وأخطأ السائلان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This situation exemplifies corruption on earth or unjust fighting; believers may not remain silent in such a case.
rows.anchor: وإنما المورد من مصاديق الفساد في الأرض أو الاقتتال عن بغي ولا يجوز للمؤمنين أن يسكتوا فيه

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Majmaʿ glosses fitna as shirk and says this interpretation is transmitted from Abū ʿAbd Allāh.
rows.anchor: قال أي شرك، قال وهو المروي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: العلاء بن الفضيل
rows.claim: Al-ʿAlāʾ b. al-Fuḍayl reports asking whether Muslims may initiate combat in a sacred month; the answer permits fighting back if polytheists violate its sanctity, citing the rule of reciprocal sacred months.
rows.anchor: عن العلاء بن الفضيل، قال سألته عن المشركين أيبتدأهم المسلمون بالقتال في الشهر الحرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses classify people by hypocrisy versus sincerity in faith, whereas the preceding verses classify them by whether they seek this world or the next; the connection to the Hajj verses is clear.
rows.anchor: تشتمل الآيات على تقسيم آخر للناس من حيث نتائج صفاتهم، كما أن الآيات السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase ‘in worldly life’ grammatically modifies ‘pleases you’: the speech pleases in this life because judgment here rests on appearances.
rows.anchor: وقوله { في الحياة الدنيا } ، متعلق بقوله { يعجبك }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People cannot see inner realities directly while living in this world; they can infer something of them only from their effects.
rows.anchor: وأما الباطن والسريرة فتحت الستر ووراء الحجاب، لا يشاهده الإنسان

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite speaks attractively of upholding truth, caring for people, and advancing religion and the community, yet is truth’s fiercest opponent.
rows.anchor: يتكلم بما يعجبك كلامه، من ما يشير به إلى رعاية جانب الحق، والعناية بصلاح الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ald is the superlative of l-d-d, ‘to contend fiercely’; al-khiṣām means severe disputation, with akhṣām as the plural of khaṣm.
rows.anchor: أفعل التفضيل من لد لدودا إذا اشتد خصومة، والخصام جمع خصم كصعب وصعاب

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative grammatical account treats khiṣām as a verbal noun rather than a plural.
rows.anchor: وقيل الخصام مصدر، ومعنى ألد الخصام أشد خصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tawallā means taking authority and power; the next verse supports this, since the man’s worldly standing is acquired through sin and hypocrisy hidden beneath his speech.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده قوله تعالى في الآية التالية { أخذته العزة بالإثم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense is turning away from the conversation: after leaving, he changes from professed concern for good to pursuing corruption.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون التولي بمعنى الإعراض عن المخاطبة والمواجهة، أي إذا خرج من عندك كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Destroying crops and offspring explains earthly corruption: human survival depends on food and reproduction, and plants sustain both people and animals, so their ruin destroys humanity.
rows.anchor: ولما كان قوام النوع الإنساني من حيث الحياة والبقاء بالتغذي والتوليد فهما الركنان القويمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disfavored corruption is not natural becoming and decay: the created order entails change, death, and life together, so God cannot hate what He decrees.
rows.anchor: المراد بالفساد ليس ما هو فساد في الكون والوجود الفساد التكويني فإن النشأة نشأة الكون والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The corruption God rejects is corruption under religious law: revelation reforms deeds and character, bringing balance and happiness to human society in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: وإنما هو الفساد المتعلق بالتشريع فإن الله إنما شرع ما شرعه من الدين ليصلح به أعمال عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hypocrite’s apparent reform masks corruption: he distorts words, changes divine rulings, and alters religious teaching, damaging morals, unity, religion, humanity, and worldly life.
rows.anchor: يفسد بما ظاهره الإصلاح بتحريف الكلمة عن موضعها، وتغيير حكم الله عما هو عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: History bears out the passage in rulers whose handling of religion and worldly affairs harmed religion, lowered Muslims, and divided the community; destruction begins with religion and follows with humanity.
rows.anchor: وقد صدق هذه الآيات ما جرى عليه التاريخ من ولاية رجال وركوبهم اكتاف هذه الأمة الإسلامية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some narrations, to be discussed later, interpret the ruined crops and progeny as religion and humanity.
rows.anchor: ولهذا فسر قوله ويهلك الحرث والنسل في بعض الروايات بهلاك الدين والإنسانية كما سيأتي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ʿizza is dignity or might, and al-mihād is a bed or resting place.
rows.anchor: العزة معروفة، والمهاد الوطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition bi is most naturally attached to al-ʿizza: this is dignity acquired through sin, reflecting the hypocrisy of a heart that disagrees with its tongue.
rows.anchor: المعنى إنه إذا أمر بتقوى الله أخذته العزة الظاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: True dignity comes from God, as 3:26, 63:8, and 4:139 state; this man’s apparent worldly status is counterfeit dignity gained through sin, not a divine gift.
rows.anchor: أن العزة المطلقة إنما هي من الله سبحانه كما قال تعالى تعز من تشاء وتذل من تشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects attaching bi-l-ithm to akhadathu as either causative or causal: that would call the condition true dignity, whereas ‘dignity through sin’ marks it as false.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن قوله { بالإثم } ليس متعلقا بقوله { أخذته }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surrounding passage concerns divorce rulings, waiting periods, and a divorced woman nursing her child, with some rulings on prayer interposed.
rows.anchor: بيان الآيات في احكام الطلاق والعدة وإرضاع المطلقة ولدها، وفي خلالها شيء من أحكام الصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭalāq originally means releasing a restraint; it was transferred metaphorically to release from marriage and became the established literal term through frequent use.
rows.anchor: أصل الطلاق التخلية عن وثاق وتقييد، ثم استعير لتخلية المرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarabbus means waiting or detention; ‘with themselves’ indicates withholding from men, the divorce waiting period that prevents mixing of reproductive fluids and confused lineages.
rows.anchor: والتربص هو الانتظار والحبس، وقد قيد بقوله تعالى بأنفسهن، ليدل على معنى التمكين من الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The waiting-period rationale is preserving lineage, but a legal rationale need not apply in every case because rulings follow predominant interests rather than universal ones.
rows.anchor: ويزيد على معنى العدة الإشارة إلى حكمة التشريع، وهو التحفظ عن اختلاط المياه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declarative wording is intended as a command and emphasizes the obligation to observe the waiting period.
rows.anchor: والجملة خبر أريد به الإنشاء تأكيدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾ can mean either purity or menstruation and is called a contronym; because its root sense is gathering blood, followed by its discharge, al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers purity.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا فالأظهر أن يكون معناه الطهر لكونه حالة جمع الدم ثم استعمل في الحيض لكونه حالة قذفه بعد الجمع

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib says qurʾ technically names entry into menstruation after purity and collectively denotes purity with the following menstruation, then can name either separately; neither uninterrupted purity without blood nor continuous bleeding is called dhāt qurʾ.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب في مفرداته والقرء في الحقيقة اسم للدخول في الحيض عن طهر ولما كان اسما جامعا للأمرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾ’s root sense of gathering is supported by the Qurʾān’s use of qurʾān and qurʾānah for collection and recitation in 75:16–18 and 17:106.
rows.anchor: ويشعر بأن الأصل في مادة قرء الجمع، قوله تعالى

words: أَن يَكْتُمْنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِىٓ أَرْحَامِهِنَّ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition covers concealing menstruation or a child in the womb to shorten the waiting period or harm the husband by obstructing his return.
rows.anchor: المراد به تحريم كتمان المطلقة الدم أو الولد استعجالا في خروج العدة أو إضرارا بالزوج

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faith condition does not make faith a prerequisite for the law; it exhorts believers to comply by framing the ruling as inherent to faith.
rows.anchor: مع عدم اشتراط أصل الحكم بالإيمان نوع ترغيب وحث لمطاوعة الحكم والتثبت عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baʿūla is the plural of baʿl, a male spouse while the couple remains married; its associations of height, strength, and steadiness underlie uses for a rider, elevated land, an idol, and a mature palm.
rows.anchor: البعولة جمع البعل وهو الذكر من الزوجين ما داما زوجين وقد استشعر منه معنى الاستعلاء والقوة والثبات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to the divorced women, but the return right applies only to revocably divorced women, during the waiting period, not irrevocably divorced women.
rows.anchor: إلا أن الحكم خاص بالرجعيات دون مطلق المطلقات الأعم منها ومن البائنات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition requires the husband to intend reconciliation and reform, barring return intended to injure the woman, as the following verse also forbids.
rows.anchor: والتقييد بقوله إن أرادوا إصلاحا، للدلالة على وجوب أن يكون الرجوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative ‘more entitled’ implies a comparison with other suitors, but only the first husband can actually resume the marriage; its implied sense is ‘more entitled to them than others.’
rows.anchor: ومن هنا يظهر أن في الآية تقديرا لطيفا بحسب المعنى، والمعنى وبعولتهن أحق بهن من غيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparative entitlement itself confirms that the rule concerns revocable divorces, since irrevocable divorce permits no return.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأحقية إنما تتحقق في الرجعيات دون البائنات التي لا رجوع فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse addresses consummated marriages of menstruating women who are not pregnant; other verses govern unconsummated marriages, minors, menopausal women, and pregnant women.
rows.anchor: والآية خاصة بحكم المدخول بهن من ذوات الحيض غير الحوامل، وأما غير المدخول بها والصغيرة واليائسة والحامل فلحكمها آيات أخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʿrūf is what people recognize through the acquired taste of their social life; under Islam’s natural order it also embraces reason, religious law, good character, and proper etiquette.
rows.anchor: المعروف هو الذي يعرفه الناس بالذوق المكتسب من نوع الحياة الاجتماعية المتداولة بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage repeats maʿrūf twelve times to ensure divorce and related conduct follow sound, natural standards.
rows.anchor: وقد كرر سبحانه المعروف في هذه الآيات فذكره في اثني عشر موضعا اهتماما بأن يجري هذا العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Natural social order requires equal rights and duties, while recognizing each person’s distinct contribution and status; Islam gives women what it places upon them while preserving their social weight in marriage and procreation.
rows.anchor: فجعل لها مثل ما جعل عليها مع حفظ ما لها من الوزن في الحياة الاجتماعية في اجتماعها مع الرجل للتناكح والتناسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The degree is a rank that qualifies the preceding equality: women receive like obligations and rights while men retain their degree over them; he promises fuller treatment later.
rows.anchor: والدرجة المنزلة. ومن هنا يظهر أن قوله تعالى { وللرجال عليهن درجة } ، قيد متمم للجملة السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marrah means one occurrence or instance of an act, from murr, passage; dafʿah, karrāh, and nazlah have parallel form and sense.
rows.anchor: المرة بمعنى الدفعة مأخوذة من المرور للدلالة على الواحد من الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tasrīḥ originally means releasing livestock to graze and is metaphorically releasing a wife by not taking her back until her waiting period ends.
rows.anchor: والتسريح أصله الإطلاق في الرعي مأخوذ من سرحت الإبل وهو أن ترعيه السرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two divorces are those permitting revocation, as the following instruction to retain or release shows; the third is the divorce described in 2:230.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالطلاق في قوله تعالى الطلاق مرتان، الطلاق الذي يجوز فيه الرجعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent sense is release after either of the first two divorces once the waiting period expires, though al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī prefers the third divorce as the more apparent reading.
rows.anchor: والمراد بتسريحها بإحسان ظاهرا التخلية بينها وبين البينونة وتركها بعد كل من التطليقتين الأوليين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers that release with kindness means the third divorce, with 2:230 detailing what this verse states generally.
rows.anchor: وإن كان الأظهر أنه التطليقة الثالثة كما هو ظاهر الإطلاق في تفريع قوله فإمساك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A husband must not use revocation to hurt his wife by repeatedly divorcing and taking her back near the end of the waiting period; proper retention restores harmony and tranquility.
rows.anchor: فإن الإمساك والرد إلى حبالة الزوجية ربما كان للإضرار بها وهو منكر غير معروف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Release too can be driven by anger or revenge; valid release follows what people recognize and the law approves, as the next verse states.
rows.anchor: والذي يجوزه هذه الشريعة أن يكون تسريحا بنوع يتعارفه الناس ولا ينكره الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Release is qualified by iḥsān, a standard beyond maʿrūf, because the sentence is followed by language that requires it.
rows.anchor: وأما ما في هذه الآية أو تسريح بإحسان، حيث قيد التسريح بالإحسان وهو معنى زائد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage shifts address from plural to singular in ‘these are God’s limits,’ back to plural in ‘do not transgress them,’ then singular again; this enlivens attention and prevents inattentive listening.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية التفات عن خطاب الجمع في قوله { ولا يحل لكم } ، وقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This gives the ruling on the third divorce: the woman is forbidden to her former husband until she marries another husband.
rows.anchor: بيان لحكم التطليقة الثالثة وهو الحرمة حتى تنكح زوجا غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse negates permissibility of the woman herself, although contract and intercourse are what are prohibited, thereby indicating that both are forbidden.
rows.anchor: وقد نفى الحل عن نفس الزوجة مع أن المحرم إنما هو عقدها أو وطئها ليدل به على تعلق الحرمة بهما جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ‘Until she marries another husband’ indicates both a marriage contract and intercourse with that husband.
rows.anchor: وليشعر قوله تعالى حتى تنكح زوجا غيره، على العقد والوطء جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the second husband divorces her, the woman and first husband may remarry by mutual agreement and a new contract; this mutual return differs from the husband’s unilateral revocation after the first two divorces.
rows.anchor: فإن طلقها الزوج الثاني فلا جناح عليهما أي على المرأة والزوج الأول أن يتراجعا إلى الزوجية بالعقد بالتوافق من الجانبين

words: إِن ظَنَّآ أَن يُقِيمَا حُدُودَ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The former spouses may remarry only if they think they can uphold God’s limits.
rows.anchor: وذلك إن ظنا أن يقيما حدود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses the explicit noun ‘limits’ where a pronoun could stand, because the limits intended here are distinct from the prior ones.
rows.anchor: ووضع الظاهر موضع المضمر في قوله تعالى { وتلك حدود الله } ، لأن المراد بالحدود غير الحدود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The concise verse contains fourteen pronouns with different, interwoven referents without making its expression difficult or obscure.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية من عجيب الإيجاز ما يبهت العقل، فإن الكلام على قصره مشتمل على أربعة عشر ضميرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses use many indefinite nouns and euphemisms smoothly: for example, ‘what you gave’ means the marriage gift, ‘what she ransoms’ means khulʿ payment, and ‘they return’ means a new contract.
rows.anchor: وقد اشتملت هذه الآية والتي قبلها على عدد كثير من الأسماء المنكرة والكنايات من غير رداءة في السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses balance retention against release and contrast fearing failure to uphold God’s limits with thinking they can uphold them; they also vary ‘do not transgress’ and ‘whoever transgresses.’
rows.anchor: وفي الآيتين حسن المقابلة بين الإمساك والتسريح، وبين قوله { أن يخافا أن لا يقيما حدود الله } ، وبين قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reaching the waiting-period term means approaching its end, not completing it, since retaining or releasing her has no sense after the period ends; 2:231 confirms this.
rows.anchor: المراد ببلوغ الأجل الإشراف على انقضاء العدة، فإن البلوغ كما يستعمل في الوصول إلى الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse forbids revocation to harm a woman, just as it forbids taking back the marriage gift at divorce outside the khulʿ procedure.
rows.anchor: نهى عن الرجوع بقصد المضارة، كما نهى عن التسريح بالأخذ من المهر في غير الخلع

words: وَمَن يَفْعَلْ ذَٰلِكَ فَقَدْ ظَلَمَ نَفْسَهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Harmful retention contradicts marriage’s purpose of shared happiness, tranquility, and mutual support in meeting natural needs; it wrongs the husband himself by turning him from human nature.
rows.anchor: فإن التزوج لتتميم سعادة الحياة، ولا يتم ذلك إلا بسكون كل من الزوجين إلى الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s laws are not empty formal rules but serve public welfare, human happiness, moral formation, purification, and sound knowledge; following outward rules while discarding these ends mocks the divine signs.
rows.anchor: لم يشرع ما شرعه لهم من الأحكام تشريعا جامدا يقتصر فيه على أجرام الأفعال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing can mean religion itself and the happiness attained through its laws; ‘the Book and wisdom’ then explain this as the outward rulings and their inward wisdom.
rows.anchor: المراد بالنعمة في قوله تعالى { واذكروا نعمة الله عليكم } ، نعمة الدين أو حقيقة الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls religious happiness a blessing in 5:3, 5:6, and 3:103; this supports reading the blessing here as religion or its felicity.
rows.anchor: فإن الله تعالى سمى السعادة الدينية نعمة، كما في قوله تعالى

words: وَمَآ أَنزَلَ عَلَيْكُم مِّنَ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ وَٱلْحِكْمَةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the blessing may encompass all divine, including created, blessings; the passage then recalls life’s goods and marital harmony, urging reflection and warning against corrupting life’s fullness.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن يكون المراد بالنعمة مطلق النعم الإلهية، التكوينية وغيرها، فيكون المعنى

words: وَٱتَّقُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ وَٱعْلَمُوٓا۟ أَنَّ ٱللَّهَ بِكُلِّ شَىْءٍ عَلِيمٌۭ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s complete knowledge should keep outward conduct from contradicting inward intent and prevent people from destroying the inner religion while appearing to uphold its outward form.
rows.anchor: حتى لا يخالف ظاهركم باطنكم، ولا تجترؤوا على الله بهدم باطن الدين في صورة تعمير ظاهره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAḍl means to obstruct or prevent; here it is the blocking of women from remarrying their former husbands.
rows.anchor: العضل المنع، والظاهر أن الخطاب في قوله فلا تعضلوهن، لأوليائهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees are the women’s guardians and equivalent people whose opposition they cannot disregard; ‘their husbands’ refers to their former husbands.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الخطاب في قوله فلا تعضلوهن، لأوليائهن ومن يجري مجراهم ممن لا يسعهن مخالفته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guardians must not prevent a woman, after her waiting period, from remarrying her former husband when they mutually agree acceptably; this does not establish that a guardian is required for a valid marriage.
rows.anchor: فالآية تدل على نهي الأولياء ومن يجري مجراهم عن منع المرأة أن تنكح زوجها ثانيا بعد انقضاء العدة
